zh.title: 英國空軍教練機威爾斯墜毀兩飛行員彈射
zh.summary: 英國空軍Hawk T2教練機墜毀；兩名飛行員彈射受傷
body: 英國皇家空軍（Royal Air Force，RAF）一架Hawk T2先進噴射教練機，於2026年9月23日下午在威爾斯北部安格爾西島的RAF Valley（RAF）基地附近墜毀，兩名飛行員均成功彈射。警方表示，傷勢被認為是輕傷。
英國皇家空軍發言人在給媒體的聲明中表示：「一起涉及RAF T2 Hawk飛機的事件發生在Anglesey附近，該飛機從RAF Valley起飛。調查正在進行中，我們目前將不會進一步評論。」
RAF表示，兩名飛行員在彈射後不久被尋獲。北威爾斯警察表示，員警正在回應一起涉及RAF訓練機的事件，地點位於Anglesey的Pencarnisiog一帶。RAF、北威爾斯消防救援服務、威爾斯救護服務及Helimed空中救護車均抵達現場。
警方指出，兩名飛行員正在接受治療，傷勢推定為輕傷。截至聲明時，沒有更廣泛的損害或傷亡報告。北威爾斯消防救援服務後來表示，墜機地點的火勢已受到控制，並呼籲公眾避開該區域。
RAF Valley是第4飛行訓練學校的基地，該校使用Hawk T2為颱風與F-35B訓練飛行員。此事件前，該校使用機器28架Hawk T2，但其可靠性一直存在問題。2023年1月，RAF在Hawk T2引擎問題後一度暫停其飛行，問題據報導與勞斯萊斯Turbomeca Adour Mk 951引擎葉片磨損有關。
此次損失正值英國國防部尋求Hawk後續機型之際，2025年戰略國防檢討報告呼籲以更具成本效益的高速噴射教練機取代Hawk T1與T2。2026年8月7日，該部門就新的高階噴射教練機發布了資訊請求，涵蓋訓練機隊及紅箭飛行表演隊。

en.title: UK RAF Hawk T2 crashes near RAF Valley (RAF) in Wales; both pilots eject
en.summary: RAF Hawk T2 crashed in Wales; both pilots ejected with likely minor injuries
body: A Royal Air Force Hawk T2 advanced jet trainer crashed near RAF Valley (RAF) on the island of Anglesey, North Wales, in the afternoon of September 23, 2026. Both pilots ejected and police said their injuries were thought to be minor.

An RAF spokesperson said in a statement: "An incident involving an RAF T2 Hawk aircraft, flying out of RAF Valley, occurred near Anglesey. An investigation is underway and we will not comment further at this time."

The RAF said both pilots were located shortly after ejecting. North Wales Police said officers were responding to an incident involving an RAF training aircraft in the Pencarnisiog area of Anglesey. The RAF, North Wales Fire and Rescue Service, the Welsh Ambulance Service and the Helimed air ambulance were also at the scene.

The force said the two pilots were being treated for what were thought to be minor injuries. As of its statement, there were no reports of any wider damage or injuries. North Wales Fire and Rescue Service later said the fire at the crash site was under control.

RAF Valley is home to No. 4 Flying Training School, which uses the Hawk T2 to prepare pilots for the Typhoon and the F-35B. Before the crash, the school operated a fleet of 28 Hawk T2 aircraft, which has had persistent availability problems. In January 2023, RAF temporarily paused Hawk T2 flying after an engine issue on the runway at RAF Valley.

The loss comes as the UK Ministry of Defence looks for a successor to the Hawk, with the 2025 Strategic Defence Review calling for the Hawk T1 and T2 to be replaced. On August 7, 2026, the ministry published a request for information for a new advanced jet trainer covering the training fleet and the Red Arrows.
